stories.title: Nintendo Rules Out Further Switch 2 Price Rises as Console Sales and Profit Fall
stories.summary: Nintendo has ruled out further Switch 2 price rises while reporting falling console sales and reduced profit.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Nintendo Rules Out Further Switch 2 Price Rises as Console Sales and Profit Fall
sources.text: Nintendo has ruled out further Switch 2 price rises while reporting falling console sales and reduced profit. According to Bloomberg , operating profit fell 16% to 73.9 billion ‌yen (approx. $467 million) during the three months to September 30, off the back of a 15% decline in sales. CNBC said Nintendo sold 2.67 million Switch 2 units in the quarter, down 41% from the same period last year and down from the 3.82 million units that were sold during the first quarter of the current financial year (April to June 2026). Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 in September, fueled by the ongoing ‘RAMpocalypse’ that has also seen Microsoft and Sony raise the price of their consoles. Despite this, Reuters reported that Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa insisted Nintendo had enough memory to meet its forecasted Switch 2 sales of 16.5 million units for the financial year ending March 2027, and is not considering further price changes. Nintendo launches the Ocarina of Time remake today, and investors are hoping it will boost sales of the Switch 2 during the holiday sales season. Reuters said that investors remain concerned that the memory situation, as well as a “lack of high-profile titles” for Switch 2 this year, could negatively affect the console's momentum. Nintendo's financial report reveals data for the first half of the current financial year, (from April to September 2026). During that six month period, Nintendo sold 6.49 million Switch 2 units, down from the 10.36 million it sold during the same period last year. But there's important context to note here. Lifetime sales of the Switch 2 are now 26.35 million, which means it’s still outpacing the original Switch in terms of launch aligned sales (the first six quarters after release). It’s also worth noting that the Switch 2 enjoyed a record-breaking launch, fueled by ample stock availability, that saw it become the fastest-selling console of all time , so it was always going to be up against tough comparisons during its second year. And countering apparent concern from investors, shares in Nintendo jumped 8.13% today following the release of the Ocarina of Time remake and the company's financial report. As for video game sales, Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream sold 8.81 million units, Rhythm Heaven Groove sold 2.89 million units, and Splatoon Raiders sold 2.42 million units. Mario Kart World, which launched alongside the Switch 2 last year, “continued to sell steadily,” Nintendo said, shifting a further 1.78 million units during the two quarters. Elsewhere, StarFox, released in June, sold 1.17 million units, and Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, released in September, sold 1.34 million units. The expectation is that Nintendo will have some big hitters for Switch 2 in 2027, including, fans hope, the next mainline Super Mario game. Pokémon Winds & Pokémon Waves are confirmed for next year. “Nintendo’s only real blockbuster this fiscal year is the Ocarina Of Time remake," Serkan Toto, CEO of Kantan Games, told CNBC . "It’s not enough to make investors happy, especially after the device is now as expensive as it is. “It’s getting harder and harder to sell video game hardware these days, and only hits help. Nintendo must step on the gas and deliver more big games next fiscal year to make sure the Switch 2 momentum continues.” Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Switch 2 sales dropped 37% this summer, mostly before the price hike hit; Nintendo now expects sales to slump 16.9% in console's second year
sources.text: The Switch 2 is still comfortably ahead of the Switch in its first year, but it might not be ahead by its second. Switch 2 sales have plummeted over the summer months compared to this time last year; accounting for a drop of nearly four million units. That's sure to be a warning sign for Nintendo, especially as the company increased the price for the handheld across the globe at the start of September—near the end of the period it's currently reporting—which could have an impact on future sales over the busy holiday period. Nintendo has reported its sales figures from April 1, 2026 until September 30, 2026. It calls this period 'FY27 Q1-Q2' because companies are weird. Nevertheless, it's the previous six months of the year, and it's been a tough one for hardware. The Switch 2 sold 6.49 million units: a 3.87 million unit reduction compared to the 10.36 million in the same period last year. That makes a change from the original Switch, which sold in increasingly larger amounts for the first five years of its life. The Switch sold just 1.27 million units during the same period, down 32.7%, but that's not a huge surprise for the outgoing handheld. So, what to make of the dip? It is a marked reduction in Switch 2 sales compared to its bumper launch year. But that's the thing. The Switch 2 sold incredibly well in its first year; 19.8 million units sold. That's a bigger success story than the Switch. It launched just before the end of Nintendo's weird financial years but reached around 17.7 million units sold by the end of its first full year. Though it did go on to double that figure the following year, which the Switch 2 is likely to fail to achieve. Nintendo raised the price of the Switch 2 over the course of this summer period. It first announced the price increase in May, 2026; however, it didn't implement it until September 1, 2026 in most of the affected regions (US, Canada, Europe). Only Japan saw a sudden price increase effective in May, 2026. The company asks $500 for the console, an increase of $50 over its original launch price. It blamed "changes in market conditions" at the time, which is common parlance for 'memory prices are ruining everything.' The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products The most recent reporting period ended on September 30. So we don't quite know what impact that $50 price hike will have on the success of the handheld from these figures alone; however, Nintendo has reevaluated its forecast up until March 31, 2027 at just 16.5 million Switch 2 units sold; down from 19.86 million in the previous 12-month period. That's a 16.9% reduction. "Although unit sales of Nintendo Switch 2 hardware declined compared to the same period of last fiscal year, many consumers continued to adopt the system, spurred on by factors like the release of new titles," Nintendo says. And it's true, games are flying off the shelves for the Switch 2 relative to last year. Up 18.8%, from 20.62 million to 24.49 million. A certain remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time might help bump those figures, with the game coming out today. Even Switch titles are selling like hot cakes; the majority of game sales remain with the bulk of players on the last-gen console. Up 6.8%, from 61.56 million to 65.73 million. So it's not all bad for Nintendo—it still has one of the best-selling consoles on its hands. It's just been curtailed by the pesky memory and cost of living crises. Haven't we all? 3. sources.title: Nintendo says it is not considering a Switch 2 price hike
sources.text: Nintendo says it has enough memory and doesn’t need to up the Switch 2’s price Nintendo says that it has no plans to roll out another Switch 2 price hike. This comes from Nintendo ‘s latest earnings presentation, which touched on the issue of memory shortages across the industry. Nintendo says that it has enough stock to ensure that the price of the Switch 2 will not have to be increased any time soon. This comes months after the first increase saw the Switch 2’s price tag shoot up to $500 in the US , with similar increases rolled out worldwide. PlayStation and Xbox have rolled out similar hardware price increases over the course of this console generation. Every current-generation console is now more expensive than it was at launch, even the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S , which both launched in 2020. At the very least, it seems that Nintendo is aiming to maintain the Switch 2’s current price point. This is despite the company reporting a 16% decline in profits in the same earnings report.Â Much of this can be attributed to a 37% decline in Switch 2 sales . However, Nintendo also says that the console is outselling its predecessor. Despite these hardware woes, Nintendo is currently celebrating the launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. The game releases today and is already the highest-rated game of the year, as per Metacritic . Being both a Switch 2 exclusive and a remake of a game that is often held up as Nintendo’s finest hour, the company is likely expecting the title to help shift consoles going into the holiday season. As for the ongoing memory shortage leading to the hardware price increases, we can expect that to continue into 2027 . With Nintendo already committing to maintaining the current price point, it seems that the company is hoping to weather the storm until supply reaches demand once more – although there is no telling when that will be.

sources.name: The Verge Games
sources.title: Nintendo says it’s not planning another Switch 2 price hike
sources.text: Nintendo’s president says it will have ‘sufficient’ RAM as shortages drive up console prices.﻿ Nintendo’s president says it will have ‘sufficient’ RAM as shortages drive up console prices.﻿ Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa said during the company’s latest earnings call that it’s “not considering additional changes” to the Switch 2’s price, Reuters reports. The Switch 2 got a $50 price hike earlier this year, bringing its starting price up to $499. Nintendo said in Thursday’s earnings report that Switch 2 sales have dropped 37.4 percent year-over-year. According to Reuters , Furukawa also gave an update on the RAM shortage, saying, “There has been no major change to the memory situation and Nintendo is in a position to secure sufficient quantities.” Earlier this week, one of Nintendo’s Switch 2 cartridge suppliers announced it plans to stop making ROM memory to focus on memory for data centers instead. Demand from AI data centers is driving the ongoing RAM shortages that’s leading to a wave of tech price increases. Microsoft has raised Xbox Series X / S prices multiple times now, increasing the Series S’s starting price from $299 to $499. The PS5 has also been hit with price hikes, taking its starting price up to $649 .

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Nintendo Officially Addresses Switch 2 Price Hike Concerns
sources.text: Nintendo's president said the company has acquired sufficient RAM for now The video game console market is in a rough spot, and hardware prices have ballooned thanks to an ongoing RAM shortage . The PlayStation 5 currently costs $150 more than when it launched on Nov. 12, 2020. The Xbox Series X is up $300 , bringing its official price to $799.99. Even the Nintendo Switch 2 , which was released and priced after the ongoing chip crisis had already begun, got a $50 price bump on Sept. 1, 2026. Thankfully, there’s finally a bit of good news when it comes to game console prices. In a statement to Reuters , Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa said that the company can secure enough memory to avoid another price hike. Nintendo's sales fell, and operating profit declined 16% to 73.9 billion yen (roughly $468 million) in the last financial quarter, which was below analyst estimates. While Nintendo isn’t planning to raise the cost of the Switch 2 past its $449.99 price point, it may look to make more money off players by increasing Switch Online subscription costs. Reuters reported that Nintendo investors are concerned about the memory crunch and a shortage of big Switch 2 releases. Despite this, Nintendo didn’t change its full-year profit forecast or its expectation of selling 16.5 million Switch 2 units. One of Nintendo’s biggest games of the year, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, just launched to stellar reviews. “The Zelda game should sell well and give Nintendo a solid quarter, but ​the company will not release blockbuster titles until the next fiscal year,” analyst Serkan Toto said. Nintendo isn't the only company struggling to sell consoles. In July 2026, game console sales fell by a whopping 29% from the same month the previous year. Part of that decline can be attributed to price increases. Nintendo’s next big first-party game will be Metroid Ravenous , which releases on Jan. 28, 2027. Other Switch 2 exclusives currently slated for 2027 include Xenoblade Genesis , The Duskbloods , Pokémon Waves and Winds , Onyx: The Dark Grip , and Kirby and the World Beyond . Two of Nintendo's biggest games from 2026, Pokémon Pokopia and Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave , will also be getting DLC expansions next year.

stories.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is out now, and so we have confirmation of the full English voice cast for the first time.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Full English Voice Cast Revealed
sources.text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is out now, and so we have confirmation of the full English voice cast for the first time. As fans had suspected following the release of official trailers for the game, Matthew Mercer from the Dungeons & Dragons web series Critical Role, reprises his role as Ganondorf from The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. Prolific voice actor Erica Mendez plays Zelda, and Navi is voiced by Lisa Reimold. While the original Ocarina of Time, released in 1998 on the N64, did not feature any voiced dialogue, the remake features voice acting in its cutscenes. Link, of course, remains silent throughout — as he does in all the Zelda games. The full list, which IGN has verified via the credits, is below. We’ve got plenty more on the Ocarina of Time remake, including our review and our how long to beat article. Be sure to check out our expanding Ocarina of Time Remake Walkthrough for comprehensive guides on each main quest area and dungeon, plus where to get Early Heart Pieces, Early Gold Skulltulas , and Early Item Bag Expansions . sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) review
sources.text: I have a friend who first played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time back in the day, when the game was only just released and he was home from university for Christmas. This is objectively the best of all times to play any video game: not Christmas specifically, but dropped out of the regular world and faced with a few weeks filled with nothing pressing to do whatsoever. Years later, though, my friend told me that the magic of the game didn't just come down to the playing of it, but the way that the playing of it unfolded. Here's what he meant. He'd play all day, curtains drawn, family ignored, working through dungeons and pelting across Hyrule Field on Epona. Then in the evening he'd call his girlfriend, who was back with her own family for Christmas. She always wanted to know what he'd got up to that day. And not in East Sussex; she wanted to know what he'd got up to in Hyrule. So as he played he took regular breaks to tell someone else about what he had encountered, and what he had discovered, and what he had yet to overcome. It is my bright delight today to be able to tell you that, around thirty years later, having just revisited the game in Nintendo's new remake, Ocarina of Time is still worth telling people about. It's still an adventure so surprising, so satisfying, so moving that I need to talk about it. Here's the thing, though. Despite the game being a cast-iron masterpiece, this reaction was something of a surprise to me. Or rather, it was a surprise precisely because the game was a cast-iron masterpiece. In truth, a couple of weeks ago I wasn't really aching to head back to Ocarina of Time after all these years. I kind of dreaded having to slog through an echoing, once-great game and summon a thousand words of measured reverence afterwards. Thankfully I had forgotten two things. The first is that I am an idiot, which means that I had failed to realise that any chance to replay a Zelda should be leapt at. And secondly, it turns out that I'd forgotten exactly what kind of masterpiece Ocarina of Time is. And along with that last point - and we'll get to this properly in a bit - I hadn't realised that there's a secret ingredient to this specific remake that has proved absolutely essential to its greatness, and that has nothing at all to do with the code running on the Switch 2 . Let's deal with remake duties here. This is more or less the game that people played back in 1998. The beats of the adventure, with Link travelling between different eras of Hyrule in order to defeat Ganon, remain the same. You still start in Kokiri Forest and you still ride Epona over the fence at Lon Lon Ranch in one of the great heart-racing, skin-prickling moments in all of art. If you're stuck in a dungeon, you can almost always use an existing guide from the N64 game to work your way through it. The game world is still broken up into little chunks that fade out and in as you move between them. And each game still begins with that unskippably evocative intro that has Link and Epona dashing over a misty hill with the moon behind them, Zelda meets Susan Cooper. Changes though? For one thing the whole game's been updated with modern graphics, and has ditched any and all fixed cameras for a modern system of movement on one thumbstick and camera on the other. One example: Hyrule Castle Town, in my memory at least, always had a central camera and you would pivot about its streets as if you were a horse on a circus merry-go-round. Now it's pure Frozen territory, cobbled paths racing off in every direction and you can explore them with the camera rushing behind you. The game's spaces feel less like elaborate machines that you were a mechanical part of, and more like video game spaces. Yes, from the way I've phrased that I now see that something of a trade-off has taken place here. I loved that sense you got in early 3D games that the whole thing was a clever practical trick that was forever almost about to collapse in on itself, but anyway! The new Ocarina is a game you can show kids who weren't alive in 1998 and they will feel at home more quickly. Sometimes the graphical update is really wonderful. The route to Zora's Domain, which I barely remember in the original Ocarina, is now a lovely scramble over cliffs and arcing crags. A bold smattering of 1990s Nickelodeon colours and glossy textures, meanwhile, makes Jabu Jabu's Belly a cross between a pre-millennium rave and a modern soft play. My favourite locations of all, however, are two of the mid-game dungeons. The Water Temple is now a drowned Art Nouveau palace that you could easily imagine Captain Nemo knocking around in. And the Forest Temple, which is my absolute favourite Zelda dungeon of all time, is a parquet-floored murder mansion that's been overtaken by trees. Dark wood-panelled corridors and weird bits of church sticking out of the foliage. It's the kind of place you'd hear a weird crime podcast about. Trade-offs, however. My wife, a huge fan of the original game, would wander in and out as I played, and often felt the game she remembered was a little more characterful in its visuals. The moment you fight Dark Link, for example, has lost a little of its glitchy liminality, although the staging, with an old tree in the middle of a vast smoky room, is still wonderfully strange. Towards the end of the game, with the trip into Gerudo territory, you could also occasionally be forgiven for wondering if you'd stepped into one of a dozen third-person Unreal games in development at the moment. It's pleasant to look at, but it sometimes doesn't look specifically like Zelda anymore. All that, and some strange character models that inevitably I learned to love, don't really matter very much, however. Not least because a handful of clever tweaks elsewhere mean that Ocarina now races along at an astonishing clip. And all this with a careful paring back of intrusions from Navi the fairy and the owl, who were both there in the original game to help move yo

sources.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was co-developed by Xenoblade studio Monolith Soft
sources.text: The developer has assisted on almost every mainline Zelda since Skyward Sword Xenoblade developer Monolith Soft has confirmed that it was involved in the development of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake . Monolith Soft has been majorly involved in the development of Zelda titles over the last 15 years, so much so that Daiki Iwamoto, general manager for the Zelda series, said he'd like to see the studio lead its own Zelda game . And Monolith Soft's previous efforts with the series led to speculation that Ocarina of Time remake would be developed by the studio – especially when it's adept at making graphically intensive titles for their given systems – similar to how Grezzo developed Zelda remakes before creating its own unique title with Echoes of Wisdom. It looked like this would be the case when a Norwegian retailer listed the studio as the remake's developer, but it was since revealed that development of the remake was happening internally at Nintendo. However, upon the release of the game, the Monolith Soft Twitter account revealed that the studio was involved in the development, with it citing game design, programming, and graphics roles on the title. While the studio has been most well-known for creating and developing the Xenoblade Chronicles games over the last decade and a half, Monolith Soft has been one of the biggest MVPs in Nintendo history. Since 2008 with Super Smash Bros. Brawl, Monolith Soft has helped develop a ton of Nintendo's biggest titles, including Mario Kart World, every Splatoon game, and Animal Crossing: New Horizons. But its biggest contribution has been to The Legend of Zelda, where the studio assisted with Skyward Sword, A Link Between Worlds, Breath of the Wild, and Tears of the Kingdom . I do hope that Iwamoto's wish comes to fruition, because having Grezzo handling 2D Zelda and Nintendo handling the open-world titles, it'd be great to have a third studio handling development of more traditional 3D Zeldas in the vein of Ocarina of Time. Check out our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review to see why it's the highest-rated game of 2026. You can also read our Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock live blog if you're keen to grab one of Nintendo's fancy new consoles for the game's launch. Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week Scott has been freelancing for over four years across a number of different gaming publications, first appearing on GamesRadar+ in 2024. He has also written for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, VG247, Play, TechRadar, and others. He's typically rambling about Metal Gear Solid, God Hand, or any other PS2-era titles that rarely (if ever) get sequels. sources.title: Why is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time important to so many people?
sources.text: On the day the Switch 2 remake is released, we look at the impact the original had on those who played it, and video games as a whole Nintendoâs Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is out today, and in case you missed it, critics have been unanimously in love with it . Those who grew up with the Nintendo 64 original already know why its return is such a momentous occasion, but there will be those who werenât around at the time who may not necessarily know what the big deal is. Thatâs partly because the game suffers a bit from what I call The Beatles Effect. Some of todayâs young bucks will listen to The Beatlesâ music and, while still enjoying it, wonder what the fuss was all about because it doesnât sound massively different to some of the other music theyâve heard. In the same way, there will be some today who look at the Nintendo 64 version of Ocarina of Time and wonder why, in a world of Elder Scrolls, Elden Ring and other games starting with Eld, people are so excited about the return of a 28-year-old game that looks like it could be any other 3D action adventure. Just like The Beatlesâ music, however, Ocarina of Time was such an important milestone in the medium, not just because of the quality of the product itself, but because of how magma-hot the trail it blazed was, providing an experience that not only wrote the rulebook, but made the pencils too. Firstly, for many players it was their first true 3D adventure. Super Mario 64 often gets praise for demonstrating how revolutionary it could be to take an established 2D series and bring it into the third dimension, but Ocarina of Time was arguably an even greater accomplishment because it dealt with a more complex genre that went beyond mainly running and jumping. With only one analogue stick â this was long before the days when twin-stick controllers became commonplace â Nintendo had to figure out not only how to turn Hyrule into a polygonal environment, but also transition Linkâs swordplay into 3D in a way that didnât become a mess of spinning camera angles. The solution was Z-targeting. By holding down the Z button when Linkâs fairy chum Navi hovered over an enemy, Link would lock in on them and all movement would be based on that enemyâs position. Other games before it had attempted something similar but not identical â in the original Tomb Raider, Lara automatically pointed her gun at nearby enemies as they got close the camera didnât change, meaning you often found yourself aiming at off-screen enemies. By introducing Z-targeting, Nintendo instantly solved the issue of combat in 3D games before it really got a chance to become a major problem, and the number of new games to this day which offer some sort of enemy lock button speaks volumes about the importance of that invention. “By introducing Z-targeting, Nintendo instantly solved the issue of combat in 3D games before it really got a chance to become a major problem, and the number of new games to this day which offer some sort of enemy lock button speaks volumes about the importance of that invention.” Also important was the use of context-sensitive controls. The move from 2D to 3D didnât just mean more detailed environments, it also meant a more complicated set of potential abilities. A Link to the Past already gave Link a decent number of actions â swinging his sword, talking to people, reading signs, lifting objects, pushing blocks and the like, as well as a button for whatever was in his inventory â but Ocarina of Time added even more actions for Link to perform. He had to be able to pull levers, climb ladders, pull himself up onto ledges, jump over gaps, mount his horse, dive underwater, and much more. Assigning a separate button to all of these actions would have made the game far too complex, so Nintendo basically assigned the A button to almost all of these actions, with a prompt at the top of the screen telling players what it did at that particular moment. Like Z-targeting, it was another idea that would continue to be used for decades and still appears in games to this day, to the extent that we barely even notice it anymore when we approach a ladder in a modern game and a prompt appears saying â(X) Climbâ. These are technical innovations, however, and while they undoubtedly had a huge impact on the role Ocarina of Time played in the history of video games, it was the world Nintendo created that had an even greater impact on the hearts of those who played it. To this day the gameâs often fiendishly designed dungeons remain locked in the memories of those who explored them nearly three decades ago. While Ocarinaâs general âexplore, dungeon, repeatâ structure would be replicated in games like Wind Waker, Twilight Princess and Skyward Sword, with the greatest of respect to those games, nobody brings up their dungeons in the same way the Water Temple, Forest Temple, Lord Jabu-Jabuâs Belly and even that initial Deku Tree dungeon are often cited to this day. Add to that one of the greatest musical scores in the history of video games, with Koji Kondo âs iconic compositions offering such a steady stream of all-time classics that if you were to ever release an Ocarina of Time: Greatest Hits CD, it might as well just be the entire soundtrack from start to finish. The music was so good that it was incorporated into the gameplay, with the tunes played on Linkâs ocarina standing in for the magic spell mechanics seen in previous RPGs. The Switch 2 remake adds the option to hum the ocarina songs instead of entering them with the controller â for some players, that wonât be an issue, because the songbook has been embedded in their heart since childhood. And itâs this which is ultimately one of the main reasons Ocarina of Time is loved so much. sources.title: How to get a Shield and Sword in Zelda Ocarina of Time
sources.text: To reach the Deku Tree in the Switch 2 Ocarina of Time Remake, Link needs to get the Deku Shield and Kokiri Sword first To get the Sword and Shield in The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake is one of the earliest challenges you'll be given on the Switch 2. Link is asked to visit the Deku Tree, but you can't leave the village until you've found a Kokiri Sword and Shield. These are found at different locations around the village, and each requires different steps to be gone through. Below I'll show you got to get both, as well as the challenges that Ocarina places in front of you to sort out. The Kokiri Sword – the first weapon you'll get in Ocarina of Time – is found in the Southwest corner of the Kokiri Forest Village, via the tunnel you crawl through in the training ground next to the training dummies (the tunnel's location is shown on the map above). Once you crawl through, you'll see a chest on top of a high platform with a circular boulder rolling around it. You can make your way around the platform, using alcoves to avoid being crushed by the boulder and let it pass. At the opposite side of this arena is a ladder. Climb up it, and you'll end up on a platform that allows you to jump down to the one with the chest on. Open the chest, and you'll get the Kokiri Sword! To get a Deku Shield, you need to head to the shop in the middle of the Village, opposite Link's Treehouse. You can buy a wooden shield from the owner for 40 Rupees. To get the Rupees, you need to explore the entire village. They're scattered around everywhere, and you'll find everything you need before long. Here's some places to check: This should comfortably bring you up to what you need to buy your first shield. Keep in mind that the wooden Deku Shield is flammable, and can be destroyed permanently if it takes fire damage. If that happens, you can buy more from the village store and replace it, though of course you'll have to pay another 40 Rupees each time. Don't worry – eventually you'll reach a point in Ocarina of Time where you can get non-flammable, metal shields. © GamesRadar+. Not to be reproduced without permission. sources.title: Rockstar Celebrates GTA 6 Launch With New Gameplay Screenshots
sources.text: With Grand Theft Auto 6 now just two weeks away from its colossal November 19 release, Rockstar Games has shared a fresh batch of screenshots to ramp up the excitement ahead of launch. Featuring a variety of characters, locations and activities, the collection includes over 30 new images showcasing the sheer detail of Vice City and its surrounding areas. From bustling nightlife to criminal escapades, there’s plenty for you to take in, with each screenshot offering another glimpse into the world of GTA 6. You can check out the full selection below. The latest screenshots come directly from Rockstar Games, which took to social media to announce that Grand Theft Auto 6 is “officially only two weeks away.” To mark the occasion, the studio released over 30 new images from the upcoming blockbuster as part of the launch gallery , highlighting everything from an apparent robbery in progress to a packed bar filled with NPCs. The collection also showcases the game’s diverse environments, giving you a closer look at the lively world Jason and Lucia will soon inhabit. As we’re used to by now, the protagonists appear with different outfits across the screenshots, further highlighting the customisation options expected to be available in the game. A wide selection of vehicles, animals and background characters also feature throughout, with the game looking livelier than ever. The launch date is rapidly approaching, with preloads beginning incredibly soon , and these latest images offer another exciting look at what’s to come. If you’re eager to see more of Vice City before release, you can browse through all the new GTA 6 screenshots below. Which new GTA 6 screenshot is your favorite? sources.text: Rockstar gives us a brand new look at GTA 6 Rockstar has just released a gallery of brand-new Grand Theft Auto 6 screenshots. This gallery gives us a sneak peek at some of the locations in Leonida, as well as new screenshots of Jason, Lucia, and some of the supporting characters. This comes as we are now just two weeks away from GTA 6’s long-awaited release on November 19. That is after numerous delays, as well as fears that GTA 6 would be pushed back once again into 2027. These screenshots are mostly more cinematic in nature, so there isn’t much to be gleaned from them gameplay-wise. For that, we still defer to the gameplay reveal that was shared via Netflix in August . It adds to what has already been a very carefully crafted promotional campaign for GTA 6. Rockstar has been cautious with what it shows us, curating its reveals as to not give too much away. Of course, this was severely impacted by the unprecedented leaks that have come out of Rockstar during GTA 6’s development. The worst of which saw a leaker (or group of leakers), going by the name Cyberleek, seemingly gain access to the game months before release and share full gameplay clips online. As for official reveals, we can expect a launch-day trailer from Rockstar, but otherwise, it seems that the developer wants us to wait until the game is in our hands. GTA 6 will release on November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S . A PC port is expected some time later.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Rockstar drops a pile of new GTA 6 launch screenshots featuring dancers, combat dogs, and so many pores
sources.text: In 39 new screenshots, Rockstar flaunts exciting new genres of Florida Man. As many readers are no doubt keenly aware, we are—as of today—two weeks out from the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 . To celebrate its impending conquest of the collective attention economy, Rockstar has released a launch gallery of new GTA 6 screenshots showcasing the breadth and color of simulated life in Vice City. Totaling 39 new screenshots, the launch gallery has a bit of everything: It's got night life, it's got wildlife, and—most importantly—it's got plenty of protagonists Jason and Lucia holding guns and making their serious 'I am involved in violent crime' faces. You gotta have those. Of that bunch, I'm particularly interested in the screenshot of a gun-toting, tactical-geared Jason seemingly having stepped off a military aircraft and into a firefight, because there appears to be a dog in the background equipped with its own combat gear. Could Jason and Lucia get access to their very own D-Dog? At this point, we can only guess. Vice City being Vice City, the launch gallery features plenty of partying, showing off dance clubs, dockside dive bars, heavy drinkers, and general debaucherists of all ages. Including your Margaritaville types. Rockstar took the opportunity to flaunt the variety of its Florida Man representation, revealing all sorts of colorful individuals worthy of the mythology. In one screenshot, a scarred man with heterochromia has two varieties of dead reptile within arm's length. In another, Jason is menaced by a sort of knife-wielding human mullet. Even the cops are a form of Florida Man: There aren't many places nowadays where you can flaunt that sort of moustache/aviator combo without a hint of irony. And, I'll note, the new screens show a terrifying degree of pore fidelity—and how there's a wide range of skin care philosophies in Vice City. I'm not naming any names, but some of these guys could stand to try out a facial moisturizer. You'll thank me for it. It's nice. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. There's plenty more to pick through, from wide-angle shots of police raids and hazy meadow sunsets to high-speed chase stills and scuba diving scenes. All those remaining screenshots are in the gallery below. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on console on November 19—but we're still waiting to hear about PC . And we're being very patient and brave about it, too. sources.title: GTA 6 Officially Drops 36 New Screenshots Ahead of Launch
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 is just two weeks away After years of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto 6 is almost here. Two weeks ahead of the game's official launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, developer Rockstar Games revealed an all-new look at GTA 6 , with dozens of new screenshots that show the rich detail and breadth of Vice City. While GTA 6 looks impressive in gameplay video , Rockstar knows that its new open-world crime epic also looks stunning in stills — the latest preview of the highly anticipated game shows off its incredible attention to very specific details. Rockstar's latest batch of screenshots, 36 in total, focus largely on its protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. We see the duo pulling off bank heists, carjacking vehicles, fleeing from the police, and rubbing elbows with Leonida's scary good ol' boys. There are also some sweeter moments, as we see the couple dancing at a variety of clubs, from Leonida Keys' beachside bars to exclusive Vice City clubs. Another batch of screenshots shows more of Leonida and Grand Theft Auto 6 's supporting players. Rockstar Games highlights Vice City and its surrounding areas — Port Gellhorn, the Leonida Keys, and the Grassivers — in the new media. Again, the attention to detail in the game's tattoo artwork, hairstyles, undersea creatures, and Leonidan swamp folk is highly impressive. Heads up: Some of the images, particularly of exotic dancers and cabaret clubs, are just a little risqué. Hopefully, players themselves will get to capture elaborate screenshots like these when Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on Nov. 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X. Rockstar Games announced earlier this week that preloading for GTA 6 will begin on Nov. 10. Clear some space: You'll need more than 200 GB of free space to install Grand Theft Auto 6 . You'll also be competing with nearly 8 million other future GTA 6 players , so start your download ASAP.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Eight years ago the idea of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel had me captivated, but can Bethesda recapture the magic?
sources.text: Eight years ago, I sat at my desk enthralled. Bethesda had just released the first trailer for The Elder Scrolls 6 , a then mysteriously nameless, locationless sequel to one of the biggest games of all time, and I reckoned I'd just found the secrets to both. It was going to be set in the region of Hammerfell, I reckoned . And the city of Sentinel was a crucial factor in reasoning why. Admittedly, I'm maybe a little more horrified at my level of Elder Scrolls obsession than I am chuffed at any apparent clairvoyance. Ultimately it was a bit of a punt, launched off the back of a day's worth of fanatical hyperfocus and exactly the right amount of the old Gamer Network office's weapons-grade filter coffee. "There's not really a lot to go on here", I wrote, sagely, "but, if we had to, we'd plant our flag in Hammerfell as the location of The Elder Scrolls 6 ." Indulge me a bit and let's retread the reasoning. First, three assumptions were required in order to make any kind of guess at all: The Elder Scrolls 6 would not be set in all of Tamriel; not set outside of Tamriel; and would be set somewhere vaguely close in the timeline to the events of Morrowind , Oblivion and Skyrim - so as to make that bit of scrabbly rock and ruined castle, visible in that now infamous first teaser, at least somewhat traceable with contemporary descriptions in the lore. Then came a lot of narrowing down. Not Morrowind, Cyrodiil, Skyrim or the Summerset Isles, I decided, as we'd been to all of those too recently (I'll leave it up to you whether another eight years since Morrowind lets that one still count as remotely "recent", but still). And then not Valenwood, Elsweyr, or Black Marsh, thanks to the topography of the land in the trailer and the type of environment on show. That left High Rock and Hammerfell, the former of which we ruled out because of its relative size - on the small side for a presumably beefy new TES game - and more importantly, the architecture that seemed at odds with the sandy stone just barely visible in the structures of that first teaser. And finally: Sentinel. The city was perfectly positioned - along a coast with the sea to the right, dry mountains in the foreground, warm stone ruins to the left, no visible land beyond. Now, that setting is all but confirmed - "all but" as, technically , nothing's set in stone yet, pardon the pun. All we've since been shown is a sand dune, an Elder Scroll, the name Sentinel, and a brief quote from a Moth Priest to a Hammerfell High Queen. But we can pretty much lock it in. To the Elder Scrolls obsessive who spent that day eight years ago scurrying down endless YouTube rabbit holes and lingering on the dustiest unofficial wiki pages, the thought of a game set there ought to be tantalising. Already, even with that paper thin new teaser, there's enough to start picking at. The new trailer's quote is dated just four years after the events of Skyrim, for instance, with both that territory and Cyrodiil located right next door, making for some lovely opportunities for crossovers and references to wider events. And the quote itself is curious. As our guides team have already speculated , the notion of "A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate" gives off the faintest whiff of a time-forking Dragon Break. That being the timeline-branching, multiple-player-choice-enabling thing that happened at the end of The Elder Scrolls 2: Daggerfall, a game which took place - aha! - in the Iliac Bay between High Rock and Hammerfell. Surely, the same bay we're looking at in that original TES 6 trailer. It keeps going! The "victory" mentioned in that quote could refer to the victory won by the people of Hammerfell against a Thalmor invasion, in a conflict that - ooh! - took place around the same time Skyrim's main story was happening, and just a few years before that quote is dated. Could we get branching timelines? A tying together of the overarching Thalmor plotline that's been simmering away until now? A load of varying endings, as Bethesda experimented with so openly in Starfield ? I'm off again. Fire up the Unofficial Elder Scrolls Pages! There's such magic here, far beyond the apparent mastery Bethesda has over theory-baiting teasers for suckers like me. These games, for instance, also have an uncanny knack for joyful stupidity. There are Oblivion NPC barks out there that landed right as YouTube's golden era hit liftoff, and in turn defined an entire generation's sense of humour. I was once in a Slack channel here called # reeblereeblereeble , which was just myself and two other writers punting Imperial Watch taunts at each other to lighten the mood every couple of weeks, or whenever someone seemed a bit stressed. When I leave a gathering of old school friends I still catch myself bidding them "farewell!" with Wood Elf gusto, and giggling at the thought of being immediately squished into mulch . And none of that is to mention the design itself, which has at times been more or less unparalleled. The clockwork, systemic magic of Morrowind is extraordinary, the first hour alone a lesson - at least as important as good old over-cited Mario 1:1 - in instructional design. Within a walkable radius of the musty little settlement of Seyda Neen Bethesda gave the player every tool necessary for understanding - and subsequently playing with, then outright breaking - its entire world. With Oblivion it brought the role-playing open world to the masses. With Skyrim it expanded what our very concept of the masses means. By all accounts I should, then, be absolutely drooling at the thought of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel. But for some reason the excitement is muted. It's been like this since long before this second teaser, frankly, and for much of that time I've put it down to Bethesda itself. Bethesda Game Studios has not been on a good run. Fallout 76 might've finally recovered from its nightmarish launch, but time hasn't been hugely kind to Fallout 4 , which longer

stories.summary: Nintendo's latest financial earnings report is here, revealing healthy software sales thanks to the enormously popular Tomodachi Life : Living the Dream. Sales of Switch 2 hardware, however, are down. Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Nintendo game sales surge thanks to Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream, but Switch 2 hardware suffers big decline
sources.text: Nintendo's latest financial earnings report is here, revealing healthy software sales thanks to the enormously popular Tomodachi Life : Living the Dream. Sales of Switch 2 hardware, however, are down. As per Nintendo's 2nd Quarter fiscal earnings report , focusing on the three-month period ending 30th September 2026, Switch 2 hardware registered a big drop in sales during the first half of the current financial year (FY27). Over that period, Nintendo sold 6.49m Switch 2 units and 1.27m units of the original Switch - equating to a 37.4 percent decline for Switch 2 and 32.7 percent decline for Switch 1 compared to the same period last year. Nintendo had previously forecast a decline in hardware sales, and the company still expects to sell 16.50m Switch 2 units by the end of the current fiscal year. Nintendo software sales, on the other hand, saw a big year-on-year boost of 18.8 percent on Switch 2 (to 24.49m units) and a smaller increase of 6.8 percent on Switch 1. That's all thanks to the release of several popular first- and third-party titles over the first half of FY27. Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream was by far the most successful game with 8.81m units sold, followed by Rhythm Heaven Groove at 2.89m. Splatoon Raiders (the only Switch 2 exclusive of the three) sold 2.42m. Nintendo also highlighted a 60.5 percent year-on-year increase in digital game sales. The increase in software unit sales and the "continued weakness of the Yen" couldn't prevent the overall business from declining by 15.3 percent year-on-year, however. Other remaining releases in Nintendo' s current fiscal year include The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake (which launches today and was awarded five stars in Eurogamer's review ), Switch 2 re-releases of Pikmin 2 and Xenoblade Chronicles 3, as well as Metroid Ravenous, which arrives early in 2027 .

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Nintendo says Switch 2 sales have dropped 37% compared to last year
sources.text: Game sales are up by 18.8% compared to this time last year Nintendo has confirmed that the Switch 2 has sold 26.35 million consoles, down 37.4% from last year. In its latest financial results – which cover the period between July and September 2026 – Nintendo confirms that a further 6.49 Nintendo Switch 2 consoles were sold in the quarter; this puts the total number of consoles sold to 26.35 million since it launched last June. However, compared to the same period last year, Switch 2 sales are down 37.4%, with Switch 2 selling 10.36 million units during the quarter in 2025. The Switch 2 had a very strong first year, becoming the fastest-selling console of all time , thanks in part to people actually being able to buy the console, proving Nintendo's rumored decision to delay it for that reason to be the right one. For comparison, the original Nintendo Switch had sold 19.67 million consoles by the end of its 15th month. Sony reported in its second year that PS5 consoles had sold 19.3 million units by the end of March 2022 (16 months after launch). So while the Switch 2 is losing compared to the Switch 2, it's doing better than its contemporaries. And while Xbox doesn't reveal console sales figures, reports indicate the Xbox Series X|S had shipped around 28.3 million units by June 2024 , so it's safe to say the Switch 2 is probably outperforming it, too. Despite a fall in console sales, Nintendo says Switch 2 game sales were up 18.8% compared to this time last year. Naturally this would be the case given more people have Switch 2 consoles and there are more games, with the console only really having Mario Kart World and Donkey Kong Bananza around launch (there's also Welcome Tour and Drag x Drive, I guess). Splatoon Raiders and Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave got off to great starts, selling 2.42 million and 1.34 million copies respectively. And perhaps most importantly, Rhythm Heaven Groove sold 2.89 million copies, which means for the time being it's done better than Marvel's Wolverine ; nature is healing. Check out our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review to see why it's the highest-rated game of 2026. You can also read our Legend of Zelda Switch 2 stock live blog if you're keen to grab one of Nintendo's fancy new consoles for the game's launch. He has also written for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, VG247, Play, TechRadar, and others. He's typically rambling about Metal Gear Solid, God Hand, or any other PS2-era titles that rarely (if ever) get sequels. sources.name: PlayStation Blog BR
sources.title: 20 anos de PlayStation Store: desenvolvedores revelam os jogos incríveis que mais os surpreenderam
sources.text: PlayStation Studios e desenvolvedores de terceiros comentam os jogos mais surpreendentes. Há 20 anos, a PlayStation Store conecta jogadores a jogos de todos os tipos e estilos, de grandes aventuras de sucesso a tesouros indies e tudo o que há entre eles. Para marcar a ocasião, convidamos desenvolvedores da PlayStation Studios e de estúdios de terceiros a refletirem sobre um jogo incrível dos últimos 20 anos que os tenha surpreendido. Não necessariamente o jogo favorito de todos, mas um que eles não esperavam gostar tanto quanto gostaram, ou que os conquistou de uma forma inesperada. Você também pode conferir a seleção especial 20 Anos de PlayStation Store , onde poderá explorar ofertas de jogos e uma curadoria com os maiores sucessos escolhidos a dedo. Agora, veja o que os desenvolvedores compartilharam sobre jogos dos últimos 20 anos que os surpreenderam: “O jogo que me vem à mente é Balatro. Embora seja baseado nas regras simples e familiares do pôquer, fiquei completamente fascinado com a sensação de satisfação que vem de ver suas pontuações aumentarem cada vez mais por meio do progresso e de diferentes combinações. É um jogo verdadeiramente envolvente que me faz lembrar por que os jogos são tão divertidos de jogar.” – Naoki Hamaguchi, diretor da série Final Fantasy VII Remake, Square Enix “Dragon Quest XI: Echos of an Elusive Age me surpreendeu na primeira vez que joguei. Tudo, desde a história até o design dos personagens e o mundo, tem um charme difícil de não se apaixonar. Sempre que o caminho à frente parecia claro, o jogo destruía a ilusão com uma reviravolta inesperada. É uma jornada heroica maravilhosa, com uma personalidade muito original.” – Jonathan Burke, Diretor Sênior de Tecnologia, Santa Monica Studio “Um jogo que eu não esperava gostar tanto quanto gostei foi God of War (2018). Ainda é inacreditável para mim que a Santa Monica Studio tenha conseguido realizar tal feito no PlayStation 4. Mas o que realmente me cativou foi a história. Nos jogos anteriores, God of War 1, 2 e 3, Kratos foi, na minha humilde opinião, definido em grande parte pela raiva e pela fúria, com pouquíssima profundidade emocional. Mas God of War (2018) mudou isso de forma substancial. Os temas de paternidade, autocontrole, ruptura de ciclos tóxicos, luto e identidade não estavam na minha lista de expectativas. No entanto, ele se saiu excepcionalmente bem em todos esses aspectos emocionais. Pouquíssimos jogos conseguiram equilibrar uma jogabilidade incrível com uma história profundamente envolvente da maneira como God of War (2018) conseguiu.” – Ramone Russell, Diretor, Comunicação de Desenvolvimento de Produtos e Estrategista de marca no San Diego Studio “Eu não estava preparado para Inscryption. Eu achava que era só um jogo de tabuleiro com cartas meio sinistro, mas resolvi experimentar porque, normalmente, adoro esse tipo de jogo. Achei fascinante e envolvente a complexidade da interação entre as cartas e seus modificadores. Como alguém que trabalha com jogos que possuem narrativas profundas e complexas, gostei do quanto o jogo confia em nós, jogadores, para desvendar a narrativa enigmática (e a mecânica de jogo!) por conta própria. Inscryption faz algo incrível: começa como um jogo aparentemente simples e direto, que recompensa a persistência ao revelar novas camadas de jogabilidade E de narrativa a cada passo. Isso também é muito especial para mim, pois nosso gatinho que partiu vive agora como o Build-a-Card ‘lil toot boi’. Descanse em paz, amiguinho.” – Arne Meyer, Diretor de Cultura e Comunicação, Naughty Dog “Inside, da Playdead, de alguma forma, foi lançado há mais de dez anos. Não possui interface nem diálogos e oferece uma experiência totalmente única, sem quaisquer instruções óbvias, meticulosamente elaborada para ensinar por meio de uma ‘mão invisível’, de forma que pareça natural e sem esforço. Os aspectos visuais e sonoros refletem perfeitamente a história ambígua que faz você refletir sobre ela por semanas (ou até uma década) após terminá-la. É uma obra-prima.” – Marcus Smith, Diretor Criativo, Insomniac Games “O jogo que me surpreendeu completamente foi Sayonara Wild Hearts! Eu não costumo me interessar por jogos que tenham elementos musicais e de ritmo como parte central da mecânica de jogo. Mas assim que vi este jogo em ação, ele realmente me cativou e me envolveu com seu estilo colorido e único. Assim que me envolvi com a história, ela passou a me atrair cada vez mais para o seu mundo, bem como para o cenário incrível e dinâmico. Logo percebi que estava completamente envolvido em um jogo musical e rítmico, e simplesmente não consegui largá-lo até terminar a história. A trilha sonora incrível foi o que me convenceu de vez. Eu com certeza recomendaria este jogo a qualquer pessoa que normalmente não jogue esse estilo; foi uma experiência verdadeiramente memorável para mim.” – Bruno Velazquez, Diretor de Jogo, Santa Monica Studio “Escolhi ‘Shadow of the Colossus’, lançado originalmente em 2005 para PlayStation 2. Só com seu cavalo e sua espada, você galopa pelas planícies em busca de criaturas gigantes para derrotá-las e salvar sua amada, que está mergulhada em um sono profundo. O jogo é, essencialmente, Davi contra Golias. Severa no início, a aventura celebra a solidão heroica com perfeição, apresentando batalhas épicas, um grande feito tecnológico e uma trilha sonora que entrou para a história. Uma obra-prima.” – Nicolas Doucet, diretor de estúdio, Team Asobi “Uncharted 2: Among Thieves (2009) foi o que mais me surpreendeu quando o joguei no PlayStation 3, pois, depois de tanta expectativa gerada pela demo, o jogo entregou algo ainda mais épico e impressionante. Cada sequência foi incrível: a qualidade da produção, o carisma do elenco e a sensação de estar jogando um filme de grande sucesso. Foi tudo o que eu esperava que o jogo fosse, como um fã entusiasmado de PlayStation, ansioso para jogá-lo.” – Gregory Louden, Diretor Criativo, Housemarque Qual jogo dos últimos 20 anos mais te

sources.title: Guild Wars gets its first major gameplay update in almost 20 years
sources.text: ArenaNet and co-dev studio 2Weeks have announced Guild Wars Afterlife - the first major update for the game in nearly 20 years. Coming to PC and mobile, Afterlife will add a new dynamic dungeon that'll morph after each run, and a skill-drafting system that'll allow you to create a distinct skill bar that'll change each time you take it on. There'll also of course be a new narrative to dig into, as players find new characters to interact with, and the new region of Xotecha to explore. Afterlife is set to release on the 13th January next year, and will retail for $29.99 / €29.99 / £25.99. However, if you pre-order it between now and the 13th January, you can get it at a 20 percent discount. This is a pretty big deal: the last time Guild Wars 1 got a massive injection of new stuff to dive into was back in August 2007 with the Eye of the North expansion. Following this, ArenaNet would move on to focus on Guild Wars 2 for the most part, leaving Guild Wars 1 servers up and running during that time. However, the game has itself entered something of an afterlife following almost two decades of inaction. ArenaNet released Guild Wars Reforged - an enhanced upgrade to the original MMO - late last year. It also received a new dungeon in April, which has enticed new and returning players to dive back in. Afterlife's reveal comes as ArenaNet is juggling development on three live service games at once. You've got Guild Wars Reforged (with Afterlife) of course, the more traditional MMORPG Guild Wars 2 , and the highly-anticipated action-oriented Guild Wars 3 . All will receive updates and support simultaneously, a sign of confidence in the health of the MMO space.
